title: Hydraulic Backhoe Excavator (~200 t class)
model_title: Hydraulic Backhoe Excavator (~200 t class, diesel)

introduction.definition: The ~200 t diesel-hydraulic backhoe excavator is the primary loading unit of the bauxite pit. It sits on top of the bench, digs the friable gibbsitic ore (and blasted caprock) below or at track level with an ~11–12 m³ bucket, swings and loads ~90 t trucks in about five to six passes. High-precision GPS guidance shows the operator the ore/waste and grade-bin boundaries so that dilution is kept low.
applications: Loading run-of-mine bauxite into ~90 t haul trucks
Selective mining along ore/waste and grade boundaries (GPS bucket guidance)
Loading blasted caprock and overburden for backfill
key_points: ~200 t operating weight, ~11–12 m³ bucket, ~700 kW diesel
All motions hydraulic: boom, arm and bucket cylinders, swing and travel motors
Digs below its own track level (backhoe) — ideal for thin flat ore bodies
Truck spotted on the operator side at a short swing angle (~45–70°); double-side loading where possible
Stairway is interlocked: no swing or travel while it is lowered
Ground-engaging tools (teeth) are monitored — a lost tooth can wreck the sizer

introduction.summary: The ~200 t diesel-hydraulic backhoe excavator is the primary loading unit in the bauxite pit. It digs the friable ore (and blasted caprock) with an ~11–12 m³ bucket, swings and loads ~90 t trucks in about five to six passes. Everything moves hydraulically: the diesel drives piston pumps; joysticks pilot the control valves that feed the boom, arm and bucket cylinders, swing motors and travel motors.

steps.text: The diesel drives several variable piston pumps; the joysticks pilot the control valves.
At start-up, after the operator is in the cab, the access stairway is raised; the interlock then releases swing, travel and attachment motions. It stays up for the whole shift.

The arm reaches out and the boom lowers to drive the teeth into the bench ahead of the machine; the cut is made downward and back toward the tracks, finishing on the design floor (GNSS shows the clay contact).
The arm cylinder crowds the arm in, dragging the teeth through the ore while the bucket cylinder, through the side links and H-link, curls the bucket to fill it.
The boom raises the full bucket above the truck body while the swing motors turn the upper about 65° on the swing circle (peak below ~4 rpm — the ~200 t upper has large inertia).
The bucket opens (uncurls) to dump evenly into the body, then the machine swings back to the face for the next pass.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Productivity = payload per pass × passes per truck ÷ (passes × cycle time + truck exchange) × operating efficiency; e.g. 11.5 m³ × 0.9 × 1.45 t/m³ ≈ 15 t/pass; 6 passes × 30 s + ~40 s exchange ≈ 220 s per 90 t truck → ~1,470 t/h instantaneous × 0.75 ≈ 1,100 t/h effective (engineering estimate; design basis 900–1,200 t/h).

hydraulics.title: Hydraulic power: engine → pumps → control valves → cylinders & motors
hydraulics.description: The diesel drives several variable-displacement piston pumps. The operator's joysticks pilot the main control valves, which send oil at up to ~30–32 MPa to the boom, arm and bucket cylinders, the swing motors and the travel motors. Pump output is shared electronically so the engine is never overloaded.

selection_notes: Size the bucket to the truck (about 5–6 passes of ~15–17 t in bauxite) and to the required tonnes per hour; diesel suits a moving plateau pit (no trailing cable).
Backhoe configuration for thin, flat, selective ore; face shovel for high benches of massive ore.

site_assembly: Delivered in modules (undercarriage, upper, boom, arm, bucket, counterweight) and assembled on a level hardstand with cranes; pins, bolted joints and hoses to the OEM procedure.
working_bench_preparation: Level, drained working floor; bench height matched to the digging depth; room for the truck to spot on the operator side.
Edge protection and exclusion zones around the swing radius.
commissioning: Hydraulic flushing to the cleanliness target; relief and stall tests; cycle-time and swing-brake tests; stairway interlock and fire-suppression checks; GPS guidance calibration.

routine.task: Walk-around: teeth and adapters, hoses, leaks, track tension, stairway interlock, fire extinguishers.
Check auto-lube supply to all front-attachment pins and the swing ring gear.

periodic.task: Engine and hydraulic oil sampling, filter changes, cooler cleaning.
Final-drive and swing-reducer gear-oil change; swing-bearing bolt torque check.
Undercarriage measurement (pins, bushes, rollers, idlers, sprockets).
Structural crack inspection of boom foot, cylinder bosses and arm.
Swing bearing rock (tilt) measurement and bolt checks.

overhaul.task: Planned component change-out by life hours (typ. engine ~15,000–20,000 h, main pumps ~12,000–15,000 h; OEM/site data govern).
Bucket and lip rebuild; boom/arm structural repairs.

lubrication: Centralised auto-lube for all pins, the swing bearing and the swing ring gear; gear oil in final drives and swing reducers to schedule.

remedies: Stop loading; check the truck being loaded and the dig face; radio the sizing-station operator to watch for the tooth. The overband magnet and metal detector are AFTER the sizer and protect only the overland belt — the sizer itself is not protected. Replace the tooth and pin/retainer with the correct parts; check adapter wear

symptoms: Sudden pressure loss, oil mist, smoke, fire-suppression alarm
causes: Chafed or aged hoses, loose clamps, missing hose shields, oil-soaked insulation
remedies: Shut down, actuate fire suppression, evacuate via the stairway or emergency egress; replace hoses preventively by hours/condition, keep heat shields and clamps intact, clean oil residue
Oil analysis, pressure tests, clean coolers, change filters
NDT at known sites; approved weld repairs
Measure and rotate/replace components; minimise travel

safety: Swing radius exclusion; positive communication with truck drivers (horn signals, radio).
Never swing the bucket over the truck cab or over people; the truck driver remains in the cab with the park brake applied during loading.
Do not undercut the face or leave caprock overhangs; keep within the face-height limit.
Never stand under a raised bucket or boom; lower attachments and release pressure before maintenance.
Fire suppression and extinguishers; hot-surface and high-pressure-oil injection hazards.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Hydraulic Backhoe Excavator (~200 t class).
Walk-around: teeth and adapters, hoses, leaks, track tension, stairway interlock, fire extinguishers.
Check auto-lube supply to all front-attachment pins and the swing ring gear.
Engine and hydraulic oil sampling, filter changes, cooler cleaning.
Final-drive and swing-reducer gear-oil change; swing-bearing bolt torque check.
Planned component change-out by life hours (typ. engine ~15,000–20,000 h, main pumps ~12,000–15,000 h; OEM/site data govern).
Bucket and lip rebuild; boom/arm structural repairs.
Watch for lost bucket tooth: gap in the tooth row. Common cause: worn adapter or pin.

Watch for hydraulic hose/fitting failure → oil-spray fire: sudden pressure loss, oil mist, smoke, fire-suppression alarm. Common cause: chafed or aged hoses, loose clamps, missing hose shields, oil-soaked insulation.
Watch for slow hydraulic cycles: longer cycle times. Common cause: pump wear.
Record every inspection so trends — wear, temperatures, pressures, leaks and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: Why is a backhoe (not a face shovel) favoured for thin, flat bauxite ore?
options: It digs below its own track level and can select along the ore boundary
questions.explanation: A backhoe sits on the bench and digs down into the thin ore horizon.

questions.question: What pilots the main control valves?
questions.explanation: Joysticks send pilot signals that shift the main control valves.

questions.question: What turns the bucket cylinder stroke into a large bucket rotation?
options: The side links and H-link four-bar linkage
questions.explanation: The linkage multiplies the bucket rotation.

questions.question: Why must the stairway be raised before swinging?
options: The interlock prevents swing/travel while it is lowered — it would strike people or the tracks
questions.explanation: Access systems are interlocked with motion.

questions.question: About how many passes should fill a ~90 t truck with this machine in bauxite?
questions.explanation: Pass matching: ~15–17 t per pass into a ~90 t body.

questions.question: Productivity rises most when the operator…

questions.explanation: Short swing angle, full bucket and well-spotted trucks.

questions.explanation: People and vehicles must stay outside the swing radius.

controls: Two joysticks (ISO pattern: left — swing and arm, right — boom and bucket)
Travel pedals/levers, swing brake, stairway switch, monitoring display with GPS guidance
Pilot-control lockout (safety) lever: LOCK before starting, before leaving the seat and before lowering the stairway
pre_start: Walk-around (teeth, hoses, leaks, track tension, fire extinguisher)
Check fluid levels; confirm the face and working floor are safe
start_up: Confirm nobody is on the decks or within the swing radius; sound the horn; start with the lockout lever locked
Warm up at low idle and cycle functions slowly until the hydraulic oil reaches the OEM minimum (typ. ~20–30 °C); raise the stairway; test the swing brake and all controls
normal: Position the machine with the travel motors/sprockets at the rear, away from the face, and the tracks square to the edge
Truck spotting on the operator side, swing ~45–70°; first pass at the front of the body; never over the cab
Dig along the GPS ore/waste line; keep the floor level for the trucks
Watch for oversize or tramp steel; report lost teeth immediately
shut_down: Park on level ground clear of faces and drainage lines, bucket on the ground; idle 3–5 min to cool the turbos; stop the engine
Operate the controls to release residual pilot/accumulator pressure; LOCK the pilot lever; lower the stairway; isolate and lock out
alarms_interlocks: Pilot-control lockout (engine start only when locked; all motions dead when locked)
Stairway-down interlock: no swing, travel or attachment motion while lowered
Emergency engine stops in the cab, on the upper deck and at ground level
Travel/swing warning alarm and beacon; swing brake applied when swing is idle/parked
tips: Load the truck evenly — centre the load over the axles
Do not use the bucket to push or travel with a loaded bucket
Keep the swing short and smooth
